steps: Convert all volumes from cm³ to dm³ (divide by 1000)
Find moles of the known substance: n = c × V
Use the mole ratio from the balanced equation to find moles of the unknown
Calculate concentration of the unknown: c = n ÷ V
method_card.title: Titrations, Concentration and the Mole
method_card.content:
All titration calculations follow the same four-step pattern.

The equation: \(n = cV\) — moles = concentration (mol/dm³) × volume (dm³)

Always divide cm³ by 1000 to convert to dm³ before using this equation.

The four-step method:

  1. Calculate moles of the substance you know (concentration and volume both given)
  2. Use the mole ratio from the balanced equation to find moles of the unknown substance
  3. Convert the volume of the unknown solution to dm³
  4. Calculate concentration = moles ÷ volume

Common pitfalls:

  • Forgetting to divide cm³ by 1000 — this is the most common error
  • Using a 1:1 ratio when the equation shows 2:1 or 1:2
  • Using g/dm³ when mol/dm³ is needed — convert via Mr

exam_context.frequency: High — titration calculations appear almost every year in Separate Chemistry

gold.display: 2.0 g of NaOH (Mr = 40) is dissolved in water and made up to 200 cm³ in a volumetric flask. 25.0 cm³ of this solution is titrated against HCl. The titre is 31.25 cm³. The equation is: NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O. Calculate the concentration of the HCl in mol/dm³.

misconceptions.message: Moles NaOH = 2/40 = 0.05. Conc in flask = 0.05/0.2 = 0.25 mol/dm³. Moles in 25cm³ = 0.25 × 0.025 = 0.00625. Conc HCl = 0.00625/0.03125 = 0.2 mol/dm³.

gold.display: 5.3 g of Na₂CO₃ is dissolved in water and made up to 250 cm³. 25.0 cm³ of this solution is titrated against HCl, and the titre is 25.0 cm³. The equation is: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂. Calculate the concentration of the HCl in mol/dm³. (Ar: Na = 23, C = 12, O = 16)
Calculate the mass of hydrogen chloride (HCl) needed to make 250 cm³ of a 0.5 mol/dm³ solution. Give your answer to 1 decimal place. (Ar: H = 1, Cl = 35.5)

A student dissolves some KOH in water and makes up 500 cm³ of solution. A 25.0 cm³ sample is titrated with 20.0 cm³ of 0.1 mol/dm³ HCl. KOH + HCl → KCl + H₂O. Calculate the mass of KOH originally dissolved. (Ar: K = 39, O = 16, H = 1)

misconceptions.message: Moles HCl = 0.1 × 0.02 = 0.002. 1:1 ratio. Conc KOH = 0.002/0.025 = 0.08 mol/dm³. Total moles in 500cm³ = 0.08 × 0.5 = 0.04. Mr KOH = 56. Mass = 0.04 × 56 = 2.24 g.

bronze.display: A solution has a concentration of 0.1 mol/dm³. Calculate the number of moles in 25.0 cm³ of this solution.

misconceptions.message: Convert cm³ to dm³ first: 25.0 ÷ 1000 = 0.025 dm³. Then n = 0.1 × 0.025 = 0.0025 mol.

misconceptions.message: Convert volume first: 500 cm³ = 0.5 dm³. Concentration = 0.15 ÷ 0.5 = 0.3 mol/dm³.

silver.display: 25.0 cm³ of NaOH of unknown concentration is neutralised by 20.0 cm³ of 0.125 mol/dm³ HCl. The equation is: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O. Calculate the concentration of the NaOH in mol/dm³.
silver.equation_hint: \(n = c \times V\) then use mole ratio, then \(c = \frac{n}{V}\)

misconceptions.message: Convert volumes to dm³: 20.0 cm³ = 0.02 dm³, 25.0 cm³ = 0.025 dm³. Moles HCl = 0.125 × 0.02 = 0.0025. Ratio 1:1. Conc NaOH = 0.0025 ÷ 0.025 = 0.1 mol/dm³.

silver.display: 25.0 cm³ of 0.2 mol/dm³ NaOH is neutralised by 20.0 cm³ of H₂SO₄. The equation is: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Calculate the concentration of the H₂SO₄ in mol/dm³.
silver.equation_hint: \(n = c \times V\) then use mole ratio 1:2

misconceptions.message: Moles NaOH = 0.2 × 0.025 = 0.005. H₂SO₄ : NaOH = 1 : 2, so moles H₂SO₄ = 0.005 ÷ 2 = 0.0025. Conc = 0.0025 ÷ 0.02 = 0.125 mol/dm³.

silver.display: 25.0 cm³ of 0.15 mol/dm³ HCl is neutralised by 18.75 cm³ of NaOH. The equation is: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O. Calculate the concentration of the NaOH in mol/dm³.

misconceptions.message: Moles HCl = 0.15 × 0.025 = 0.00375. Ratio 1:1. Conc NaOH = 0.00375 ÷ 0.01875 = 0.2 mol/dm³. Use the NaOH volume for the final step.

silver.display: A student dissolves some NaOH in water and makes 250 cm³ of solution. 25.0 cm³ of this is titrated with 20.0 cm³ of 0.2 mol/dm³ HNO₃. NaOH + HNO₃ → NaNO₃ + H₂O. Calculate the mass of NaOH dissolved. (Ar: Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)
silver.equation_hint: Find conc NaOH, then total moles in 250 cm³, then mass = n × Mr

misconceptions.message: Moles HNO₃ = 0.2 × 0.02 = 0.004. 1:1 ratio. Conc NaOH = 0.004/0.025 = 0.16 mol/dm³. Total moles = 0.16 × 0.25 = 0.04. Mr NaOH = 40. Mass = 0.04 × 40 = 1.6 g.

silver.display: 25.0 cm³ of 0.1 mol/dm³ Ca(OH)₂ is neutralised by 20.0 cm³ of HCl. The equation is: Ca(OH)₂ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + 2H₂O. Calculate the concentration of the HCl in mol/dm³.
silver.equation_hint: \(n = c \times V\) then use mole ratio 1:2
